blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Repeated robotic monitoring requires localization across visits to the same environment, even if the environment changes. Such changes can substantially reduce persistent visual content, and repetitive structures can lead to incorrect cross-session correspondences. In this paper, we address visual multi-session registration of a new data recording (the query session) to a previously reconstructed reference map. Under substantial visual and structural changes, cross-session localization may be possible only for parts of the trajectory. In our approach, we therefore rely on a sparse set of reliable absolute pose constraints and combine them with within-session relative-pose information to register the complete trajectory to the reference map. We first estimate absolute alignment hypotheses through visual place recognition, local feature matching, and geometric verification. We then use sequence consensus to reject hypotheses that are inconsistent with a common query-to-reference alignment and retain the remaining poses as absolute anchors. These anchors are refined through featuremetric alignment against a Gaussian feature field and combined with within-session relative-pose constraints in a robust pose-graph optimization. We evaluate our approach on 15 cross-session experiments from the challenging HILTI26 construction-site dataset, covering substantial scene changes and difficult-to-match environments. Our method achieves 94.4% recall within 1m and 100.0% within 5m, outperforming independent image localization, which peaks at 65.3% and 70.7%, respectively, as well as direct registration of independently reconstructed Structure-from-Motion geometry. Our results show that sparse, reliable absolute anchors can provide accurate and complete trajectory registration even when reliable cross-session correspondences are available only for part of the query session.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Most robotic systems operating repeatedly in the same environment must reliably
localize in a previously built map despite scene changes.
Reliable cross-session localization and registration are therefore important for
long-term autonomy, repeated inspection and monitoring, as well as persistent
mapping [ 17 , 37 , 13 ] .
This becomes particularly challenging when changes are structural rather than purely
appearance-level, since parts of the previously mapped geometry may no longer exist,
while new structures may alter or occlude previously visible content.

blocks.en:
Construction sites are a particularly demanding instance of this problem.
Their geometry and appearance evolve as walls, installations, temporary
structures, and surface finishes are added, removed, or modified, while
repetitive and low-texture structures create additional perceptual
ambiguity [ 32 ] , further compounded by the frequent lack of GNSS
availability in indoor construction environments.
Construction progress monitoring requires repeated observations to compare the current
as-built state against earlier observations or the planned state [ 34 ] .
Autonomous mobile robots can acquire such observations, but comparing visits requires
reliable localization in a common coordinate frame.

In this work, we address visual multi-session registration in challenging,
GNSS-denied, and changing environments.
Given a previously reconstructed reference map , together with

Existing strategies often use image-based localization against an earlier

Image-based localization becomes unreliable when persistent visual content is limited
or perceptually ambiguous, while 3D point-cloud registration degrades as spatial and

blocks.en:
The main contribution of this paper is a visual multi-session registration approach for
changing environments, where scene changes and perceptual aliasing can make reliable
cross-session correspondences available only for parts of the trajectory.
Our approach combines conservative cross-session anchor selection, retaining only
absolute pose hypotheses that are geometrically verified and consistent with the query
trajectory, with featuremetric pose refinement for precise image-to-map alignment.
These sparse absolute anchors are then combined with within-session relative-pose
constraints to recover the complete query trajectory even when reliable cross-session
correspondences are only sparsely available.

blocks.en:
We make three key claims: our approach
(i) provides more accurate and complete multi-session registration than the baselines;
(ii) improves the reliability of cross-session constraints under scene change and
perceptual aliasing through conservative filtering and sequence consensus; and
(iii) improves fine image-to-map alignment through featuremetric refinement of the
verified absolute anchors.
We will publicly release our implementation upon publication.
II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
A common approach to visual multi-session registration is to localize observations
from a later session against a previously reconstructed reference map.
Visual place recognition (VPR) identifies corresponding places across sessions [ 15 , 5 , 20 , 11 ] .
Modern VPR methods range from learned aggregation approaches such as
NetVLAD [ 2 ] to scalable and viewpoint-robust descriptors [ 4 , 1 ] and representations based on large
pretrained visual features [ 15 , 14 , 3 ] .
Hierarchical Localization (HLoc) by Sarlin et al. [ 27 ] combines retrieval, local feature matching, and perspective-n-point
(PnP)-based localization and forms our image-based localization baseline.
However, such approaches rely on distinctive, persistent cross-session
correspondences and often degrade under appearance changes and repetitive
structures [ 29 , 33 ] .
In contrast, we use image-based localization to obtain sparse, reliable
absolute anchors rather than localizing every query observation.

correspondences are unreliable.
Multi-sequence maps retain observations acquired under different appearance
conditions [ 35 ] , while sequence-based VPR exploits temporal

benchmarks multi-session SLAM in construction environments [ 22 ] .
Our approach similarly exploits within-session motion, but uses sparse
cross-session anchors to register trajectories without requiring the query path

blocks.en: III Our Approach to Visual Multi-Session Registration
blocks.zh: 三. 我们处理视觉多场会议登记的办法

blocks.en:
Fig. 2: Overview of our visual multi-session registration pipeline.
We first select distinctive cross-session retrievals and establish local feature correspondences between query and reference observations.
Generalized PnP with RANSAC uses the reference-map geometry to reject correspondences that do not support a geometrically consistent multi-camera pose, producing locally verified absolute pose hypotheses.
Since a locally plausible pose may still correspond to an incorrect location, sequence consensus evaluates the hypotheses jointly with the within-session query trajectory and retains only spatially distributed hypotheses that support a common query-to-reference similarity alignment.
The resulting sparse absolute anchors are refined by featuremetric alignment against the reference Gaussian feature field and finally combined with within-session relative-pose constraints and consensus-aligned priors in a pose-graph optimization to recover the complete query trajectory.

blocks.en:
Our approach consists of five stages, illustrated in Fig. 2 .
First, we identify reliable cross-session retrieval hypotheses using visual
place recognition and distinctiveness filtering (Sec. III-B ).
Second, we establish local feature correspondences and estimate absolute pose
hypotheses using reference-map geometry and generalized PnP (Sec. III-C ).
Third, we use the query trajectory to retain hypotheses supporting a common
query-to-reference alignment, forming sparse absolute anchors (Sec. III-D ).
Fourth, we refine these anchors through featuremetric alignment against the
reference feature field (Sec. III-E ).
Finally, we combine the refined anchors with within-session relative-pose
constraints in a robust pose-graph optimization (PGO) to recover the complete query trajectory
 (Sec. III-F ).

blocks.en: IV Experimental Evaluation
blocks.zh: 四. 实验评价

blocks.en:
We evaluate our approach for registering visual sessions acquired at different
times to an earlier reference map under substantial scene change and perceptual
ambiguity.
Specifically, we evaluate three claims:
(i) our approach provides more accurate and complete multi-session registration
than the baselines;
(ii) conservative cross-session filtering and anchor selection improve the
reliability of absolute pose constraints under scene change and perceptual
aliasing; and
(iii) featuremetric refinement improves the fine image-to-map alignment of
verified absolute anchors.

HLoc performs well for observations that can be localized independently, but

present in our setting.

blocks.en: V Conclusion
blocks.zh: 五 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we presented a novel, complete visual multi-session registration
pipeline designed for challenging and changing environments such as construction sites,
without requiring reliable cross-session correspondences along the entire
query trajectory.
Our method identifies a sparse set of strongly supported absolute anchors
using visual distinctiveness, geometric verification, and sequence-level
consistency, refines these anchors against a reference Gaussian feature field,
and propagates their information through the query trajectory using
within-session relative-pose constraints.

查询轨迹。
我们的方法找出了几组 得到大力支持的绝对锚
使用视觉特性、几何校验和序列级
一致性,根据一个参考高斯特征字段来完善这些锚,

blocks.en:
Our experimental evaluation on evolving construction environments shows that
this strategy provides more complete and accurate trajectory registration than
independent image localization and direct registration of independently
reconstructed geometry.
If no sufficiently distributed consensus is found, our method rejects the
session rather than forcing an incorrect global alignment.
The results further demonstrate the importance of conservative anchor
selection and show that featuremetric refinement improves the fine
image-to-map alignment of verified absolute anchors.
